article_title: Self-regulated learning and reflection: a tool for teachers and students
citation: Avivit Arvatz, Roee Peretz, Yehudit Judy Dori. (2025). Self-regulated learning and reflection: a tool for teachers and students. Metacognition and Learning. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11409-025-09415-3
title: T-SQsrl: paired teacher and student SRL questionnaires with a triangulated reflection assessment
description: The T-SQsrl is an assessment tool comprising a teacher version (TQsrl, 31 closed-ended items plus an open-ended reflective question) and a student version (SQsrl, 15 closed-ended items), both adapted from the SRLMQ and structured on Zimmerman's cyclical SRL model. It evaluates SRL sub-processes including goal-setting, task-strategy, self-efficacy, help-seeking, elaboration, and reflection. The teacher version enables triangulated assessment by correlating self-assessed reflection with expert grading of an open-ended reflective question, while teachers provided the external assessment triangulating students' self-assessments. The article describes it as innovative in its focus on reflection skills and in allowing simultaneous assessment of teachers' and students' SRL within the same classroom or school.
requirements: External assessment of the reflection skill requires open-ended items graded by experts (for teachers) or by teachers (for students) to triangulate self-reports
constraints: The study notes validity issues with self-reports, and the sampling was a convenience sample with modest sizes adequate for initial validation only
target_learners: students aged 12 and above in grades 7–12
target_learning_goals: assessing SRL sub-processes and reflection skill for formative assessment and intervention design
examples: Ten teachers who participated in the PD administered the SQsrl to their students with parental consent to map baseline SRL before an SRL intervention, and policymakers may use TQsrl results as an indicator of a PD program's effectiveness
key_sources: Avivit Arvatz, Roee Peretz, Yehudit Judy Dori. (2025). Self-regulated learning and reflection: a tool for teachers and students. Metacognition and Learning. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11409-025-09415-3

article_title: Fostering integrated mental models of different professional knowledge domains: instructional approaches and model-based analyses
citation: Lehmann, T., Pirnay-Dummer, P., & Schmidt-Borcherding, F. (2019). Fostering integrated mental models of different professional knowledge domains: instructional approaches and model-based analyses. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-019-09704-0
title: T-MITOCAR as an automated model-based assessment tool for knowledge integration
description: T-MITOCAR (Text-Model Inspection Trace of Concepts and Relations) is an automated computer-based diagnostic tool that uses natural language expressions as input data to generate graph-based representations of learners' mental models. It measures structural and semantic similarities of verbally externalized mental models compared to a reference (expert) model using measures such as GAMMA (structural density) and BSM (balanced semantic matching). The tool relies on "the dependence of syntax and semantics within natural language" and works with a comparably small amount of text (350 words+).
requirements: Requires learners to externalize their mental models in natural language written formulations of at least 350 words
constraints: The reference model configuration may influence results; the authors note their reference model was not an argumentative text
key_sources: Lehmann, T., Pirnay-Dummer, P., & Schmidt-Borcherding, F. (2019). Fostering integrated mental models of different professional knowledge domains: instructional approaches and model-based analyses. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-019-09704-0

article_title: Promoting pre-service teachers’ knowledge integration from multiple text sources across domains with instructional prompts
citation: Inka Sara Hähnlein, Pablo Pirnay-Dummer. (2024). Promoting pre-service teachers' knowledge integration from multiple text sources across domains with instructional prompts. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-024-10363-z
title: T-MITOCAR computer-linguistic technology for modeling and comparing semantic knowledge structures of texts
description: T-MITOCAR (Text-Model Inspection Trace of Concepts and Relations) is a computational linguistic heuristic technology "developed as a means of automatically analyzing, modeling, visualizing, and comparing the semantic knowledge structure of texts." It builds graphs of concepts linked by association strengths from propositional relations, grounded in mental model theory, and compares texts quantitatively via four structural measures (SUR, GRA, GAMMA, STRU) and three semantic measures (CONC, PROP, BSM) yielding similarity values between zero and one. The study used it to compare student texts with a reference model of the four source texts.
requirements: A reference model built from the source texts against which learner texts are compared using the seven similarity measures
constraints: The article states the similarity indices measure different features and "can therefore not be treated like a subsuming scale (e.g., on a test)"
target_learning_goals: assessing semantic knowledge structure of learner-produced texts
examples: The four source texts were combined into one document and modelled with T-MITOCAR to generate the reference model against which all 109 student texts were compared
key_sources: Inka Sara Hähnlein, Pablo Pirnay-Dummer. (2024). Promoting pre-service teachers' knowledge integration from multiple text sources across domains with instructional prompts. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-024-10363-z

article_title: Quantitative comparisons to promote inquiry in the introductory physics lab
citation: N.G. Holmes & D.A. Bonn. (2015). Quantitative comparisons to promote inquiry in the introductory physics lab. The Physics Teacher. https://www.aapt.org
title: The t'-score framework: a continuous, set-paradigm measure of disagreement between two measurements relative to their combined uncertainty
description: The t'-score takes the difference between two measurements A and B and normalizes it by the combined uncertainty of the difference, defined as t'=A−B over the square root of δA²+δB². The article states that "the t'-score gives a quantitative measure of how different the two measurements are relative to their uncertainties", similar to sigma levels in particle physics. It replaces dichotomous overlapping-error-bar comparisons with a continuous scale and prescribes follow-up behaviours by score magnitude (Table 1).
requirements: Students must first be instructed in standard deviation, standard uncertainty in the mean, and t'-scores before applying the framework
constraints: The article notes it is structurally similar to Student's t but "we do not make inferences from the statistic on the t distribution"
examples: In the Pendulum for Pros experiment, students compare periods at 10° and 20° using t'-scores and conduct follow-up measurements based on the comparison
key_sources: N.G. Holmes & D.A. Bonn. (2015). Quantitative comparisons to promote inquiry in the introductory physics lab. The Physics Teacher. https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02967

article_title: ExamGAN and Twin-ExamGAN for Exam Script Generation
citation: Zhengyang Wu, Ke Deng, Judy Qiu, Yong Tang. (2021). ExamGAN and Twin-ExamGAN for Exam Script Generation. https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.09656
title: T-ExamGAN: twin-generator framework producing assessment-equivalent exam script pairs with two training strategies
description: T-ExamGAN extends ExamGAN with two generators (GA and GB) sharing the same KMLR condition and discriminator, each producing one exam script of a pair. The generators are trained alternately with a cross-entropy loss between their question distributions so the two scripts have significantly different question sets, while the discriminator enforces individual script quality. The article defines equivalence: "Two exam scripts are equivalent in assessment if student scores are comparable no matter which script is taken." Two training strategies are proposed: individual quality priority (quality first, then difference updates) and twin difference priority (difference first, then quality training).
requirements: A trained ExamGAN initialization for each generator (both trained by 1500 epochs in the experiments)
Training data of desirable exam scripts with condition c, same as ExamGAN
A specified maximum Jaccard-coefficient ratio (e.g., 30%) as the stop criterion for difference
constraints: The article notes it is less intuitive to specify the hyper-parameter psi directly, so the Jaccard-based stop criterion is used instead
target_learners: students needing formal and deferred exam versions in LMS-based courses
target_learning_goals: equivalent assessment of student performance across paired exam scripts with different questions
examples: In experiments, T-ExamGAN@S1 and T-ExamGAN@S2 each generated 100 pairs per dataset, compared against ExamGAN@500 and ExamGAN@1500 baselines
key_sources: Zhengyang Wu, Ke Deng, Judy Qiu, Yong Tang. (2021). ExamGAN and Twin-ExamGAN for Exam Script Generation. https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.09656

article_title: TecCoBot: Technology-aided support for self-regulated learning
citation: Norbert Pengel, Anne Martin, Roy Meissner, Tamar Arndt, Alexander Tobias Neumann, Peter de Lange, and Heinz-Werner Wollersheim. (2021). TecCoBot: Technology-aided support for self-regulated learning — Automatic feedback on writing tasks with chatbots. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.11881
title: T-MITOCAR generates knowledge-graph comparisons of student texts against reference texts as feedback content
description: T-MITOCAR is the software used to produce the feedback content for TecCoBot. It "constructs re-representations of knowledge from prose text through a computer-linguistic analysis, without the need to incorporate an external knowledge base", yielding knowledge graphs similar to mind maps. The graph of a student's text is compared with the reference-text graph, and feedback can inform students which key concepts their text model contains, how they are interlinked, which concepts overlap with or differ from the reference, and how concepts are linked in the assignment text.
requirements: prose text as input, either text passages like book chapters or whole texts written by students
constraints: similarity to the assignment text depends on content and on the writing task, so similarity is not always a goal parameter
target_learning_goals: conceptual knowledge about a topic studied via reading assignments
in-depth study of a topic in self-regulated learning
examples: the reference knowledge graph is generated from a textbook containing domain knowledge about the same topic as the student's text
key_sources: Norbert Pengel, Anne Martin, Roy Meissner, Tamar Arndt, Alexander Tobias Neumann, Peter de Lange, and Heinz-Werner Wollersheim. (2021). TecCoBot: Technology-aided support for self-regulated learning — Automatic feedback on writing tasks with chatbots. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.11881

article_title: Advancing Multimodal Teacher Sentiment Analysis:The Large-Scale T-MED Dataset & The Effective AAM-TSA Model
citation: Zhiyi Duan, Xiangren Wang, Hongyu Yuan, Qianli Xing. (2025). Advancing Multimodal Teacher Sentiment Analysis: The Large-Scale T-MED Dataset & The Effective AAM-TSA Model. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.20548
title: T-MED: the first large-scale multimodal teacher sentiment analysis dataset
description: T-MED is a dataset of "14,938 instances of teacher emotional data from 250 real classrooms across 11 subjects ranging from K-12 to higher education, integrating multimodal text, audio, video, and instructional information", totalling over 17 hours from more than 200 teachers. It carries eight emotion labels — neutral, anger, joy, surprise, sadness, plus the teacher-specific patience, enthusiasm, and expectation. Labels were produced by a human-machine collaborative annotation framework combining pre-trained model pre-labeling, expert correction, fine-tuning, and a five-expert voting review requiring at least four experts to confirm each label.
requirements: Annotations validated by a panel of five independent experts with a voting mechanism requiring no fewer than four experts to confirm a label
constraints: Built from public MOOC platform videos rather than in-person classroom recordings
Emotion category distribution is uneven, with neutral at 49.0% of items
target_learners: Teachers from K-12 to higher education
target_learning_goals: Recognition of teacher emotional states in classroom video, audio, text, and instructional context
examples: 250 high-quality videos downloaded from public MOOC platforms were processed with FFmpeg, Faster Whisper, and the CAM++ speaker identification model to extract the four modalities
key_sources: Zhiyi Duan, Xiangren Wang, Hongyu Yuan, Qianli Xing. (2025). Advancing Multimodal Teacher Sentiment Analysis: The Large-Scale T-MED Dataset & The Effective AAM-TSA Model. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.20548

article_title: Supporting teachers and children in schools: the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of the Incredible Years teacher classroom management programme in primary school children: a cluster randomised controlled trial, with parallel economic and process evaluations.
citation: Ford Tamsin, Edwards Vanessa, Sharkey Siobhan, Ukoumunne Obioha C, Byford Sarah, Norwich Brahm, Logan Stuart. (2012). Supporting teachers and children in schools: the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of the incredible years teacher classroom management programme in primary school children: a cluster randomised controlled trial, with parallel economic and process evaluations. BMC Public Health. https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2458-12-719
title: Teacher-Pupil Observation Tool (T-POT) for direct classroom observation
description: The T-POT is a structured real-time frequency count of defined teacher behaviours and types of teacher-child interaction, used in a sub-sample of 20 classrooms (25% of teachers) with observers blind to allocation. The article reports "Inter-rater reliability with two or three observers rating 21 primary school teachers was high (ICC = 0.78)". It codes nine teacher behaviours and seven child behaviours, including teacher negatives (e.g. reprimanding) and teacher positives (e.g. praise), and encourages comparing change between observations, particularly ratios of positive to negative behaviours.
requirements: Observers independent of the core research team and blind to allocation; no cut-off points for good or bad practice, instead comparison of change between two observations
constraints: Due to time and financial restraints in STARS, the focus of observations is on teacher behaviour rather than child behaviour
target_learning_goals: classroom management behaviours targeted by TCM, including positive approaches and reduced negative behaviours
examples: T-POT scores will be compared to the classroom management and instructional practice subscales of the Teacher sense of efficacy scale
key_sources: Ford Tamsin, Edwards Vanessa, Sharkey Siobhan, Ukoumunne Obioha C, Byford Sarah, Norwich Brahm, Logan Stuart. (2012). Supporting teachers and children in schools: the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of the incredible years teacher classroom management programme in primary school children: a cluster randomised controlled trial, with parallel economic and process evaluations. BMC Public Health. https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2458-12-719
